rationale: SkiaSurface now registers a Graphite finished callback on every frame recording (the existing GPU-stats callback when timing is supported, a plain finished callback otherwise) and counts frames submitted to the GPU whose work has not finished, exposed as SkiaSurface::gpu_frames_in_flight() with a -1 default for surfaces that do not track it. The render-skia-dawn touch is gpu_render_time.hpp (the GpuFramesInFlight counter), skia_surface.hpp (the appended virtual) and skia_surface.cpp (the callback wiring; the destructor drain already flushes outstanding callbacks). Nothing reads the count to make a decision; it feeds the gpu_acquire trace span so a trace can tell a GPU-bound frame from CPU bunching. This is Pulp's own diagnostic with no counterpart framework behaviour to backport, so it is recorded pulp-only.
